summary: This note presents a nine-step safety drill guide for protecting astronauts from space radiation events such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections. It illustrates the steps with a September 2023 CME that affected the Artemis VI lunar mission and a solar flare that concerned the International Space Station crew. The guide covers hazard assessment, shelter, dosimeter monitoring, ground communication, stress management, health checks, protocol review, drills, and ongoing education.
one_line: A nine-step guide to astronaut radiation safety, illustrated by the September 2023 solar flare and CME affecting the ISS and Artemis VI.
key_facts: Space weather is the environmental conditions in space influenced by the Sun and the solar wind, and can produce solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) that emit harmful ionizing radiation.
Astronauts outside the Earth's protective magnetic field are at higher risk during radiation events.
On September 4, 2023, Dr. Genevieve Miller, a NASA space weather expert, reported an unprecedented solar flare that concerned the International Space Station crew.
On September 11, 2023, astronaut Jack O'Neil aboard the Artemis VI lunar mission was notified of a significant CME headed towards the moon.
Jack O'Neil and colleague Sandra Lopez moved to the lunar module's shielded section during the CME; shelter areas may be lined with water, fuel tanks, or specialized materials to attenuate radiation.
Astronauts carry personal dosimeters that continuously monitor radiation exposure, and the Artemis VI crew regularly checked theirs to keep cumulative exposure below safety thresholds.
The solar flare caused some communication delays, but the Artemis VI crew stayed in constant contact with mission control.
The Artemis VI team managed psychological stress with structured rest periods, mental health check-ins, and leisure activities suited to the confined shelter.
Dr. Natasha Singh, a flight surgeon, led thorough medical evaluations of the ISS and Artemis VI crews after the solar flare.
By late September 2023, engineers and scientists including Dr. Miller and Dr. Singh reviewed the Artemis VI event and updated safety procedures.
In October 2023, NASA's astronaut corps, led by trainers such as Major Tom Harrison, began a new series of radiation safety drills based on the updated protocols.
The guide's ninth step is continuing education on the solar cycle and space weather, with NASA and other space agencies holding regular educational sessions.
